findings.text: Pre-training data is filtered for toxicity and anonymized for privacy-sensitive and other harmful content, with no safety benchmark scores reported.

source.quote:
filter the data based on criteria such as writing quality, educational value, and toxicity to ensure
its high quality. Additionally, we anonymize all privacy-sensitive data and other harmful data.

findings.text: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) places emphasis on data security and aiming for human-value alignment in most circumstances, without measured safety outcomes.

findings.text: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) training uses an exponential moving average strategy said to mitigate reward hacking, with no reward-hacking evaluation results.

notes: Technical report (arXiv 2411.02265), not a system card. No dedicated safety section and no safety, refusal, jailbreak, toxicity, bias, honesty, hallucination, or dangerous-capability numeric evals. Safety-adjacent content is only pre-training toxicity/privacy filters, an SFT data-security / human-values claim, and DPO EMA to mitigate reward hacking — all training methods/claims, so topics stay uncovered per pilot rules. AlignBench is listed with MT-Bench/Arena-Hard/AlpacaEval as preference/instruction alignment and was skipped (not a safety eval). Skipped capability results: Table 3–6 including MMLU, MMLU-Pro, BBH, CMMLU, C-Eval, HellaSwag, CommonsenseQA, WinoGrande, PIQA, DROP, C3, NaturalQuestions, ARC-C, TriviaQA, GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, HumanEval, MBPP, GPQA_diamond, AlignBench, MT-Bench, IFEval, Arena-Hard, AlpacaEval-2.0, RULER, LV-Eval, PenguinScrolls. Open-source stated without a license name. arXiv date is not a model release date.
